simple.meaning: יָקַד (yâqad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to burn.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Leviticus 6:2. Its contexts include flock, offering, kingship, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָקַד (H3344).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יָקַד (yâqad) / H3344 is traced through Leviticus 6:2, Leviticus 6:5, Leviticus 6:6, Deuteronomy 32:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

occurrences.englishText: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against Yahweh, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
or any thing about which he has sworn falsely: he shall restore it in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it. He shall return it to him to whom it belongs in the day of his being found guilty.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Yahweh: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.
For a fire is kindled in my anger,
Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.

He will break it as a potter’s vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing, so that there won’t be found among the broken pieces a piece good enough to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern.”
I will make them to pass with your enemies into a land which you don’t know;
You, even of yourself, will discontinue from your heritage that I gave you.
